name: enterprise-rag
description: Keyless retrieval-augmented generation: Azure OpenAI chat + embeddings, AI Search, Cosmos chat history, a blob document store, an orchestrator app, and API Management.
what: An end-to-end RAG stack. Azure OpenAI hosts a chat and an embedding deployment; Azure AI Search provides hybrid + semantic retrieval with integrated vectorization; documents land in blob storage; chat history persists in serverless Cosmos DB; a Python App Service orchestrates the pattern; and API Management fronts it with subscription keys and policy. Every hop uses managed identity and RBAC - local auth is disabled everywhere.
why: Teams want grounded, governed generative answers over their own content without standing up keys, secrets, or bespoke glue. This wires the canonical RAG components together with least-privilege identity and a managed API facade so it is auditable and rate-limited from day one.
potentialUseCases: Internal knowledge assistant grounded in policy and product docs
Customer support copilot over a manual / KB corpus
Contract and claims Q&A with citations
Developer portal for governed access to a shared LLM via APIM

reliability: Zone-redundant App Service and ZRS storage in prod
Cosmos automatic failover enabled in prod
Search replicas scaled for query availability
security: Local auth disabled on OpenAI, Search, and Cosmos
Least-privilege RBAC: app and search identities get only the roles they need
API Management enforces subscription keys and policy
Cosmos data-plane access via SQL RBAC, no keys
costOptimization: Basic Search + P0v3 + Developer APIM in dev
operationalExcellence: Application Insights + Log Analytics across the stack
Single template captures the whole RAG topology
performanceEfficiency: Semantic + vector hybrid retrieval improves answer quality
Embedding and chat deployments scaled independently

cost.profile: Prod profile: gpt-4o-mini @60K TPM, Standard Search x3, P1v3 x3, Premium APIM.

components.name: API Management (Premium)
components.notes: One Premium unit; Developer tier in dev is far cheaper.
